name: Treaty with the Miami, 1838 (Treaty of the Forks of the Wabash)
promises: Article 2: a reserve of about ten square miles on the Mississinewa kept for the band of Me-to-sin-ia out of the cession.
Article 3: $335,680, with $60,000 paid after ratification and the rest, after claims, in ten yearly instalments of $12,568.
Article 7: the buildings and improvements on the ceded land to be appraised and matching improvements made where the chiefs chose, the Miami keeping peaceable occupation until then.
Article 9: the boundary lines of the Miami lands in Indiana to be surveyed and marked within one year of ratification.

Article 10: the United States to guarantee the Miami forever a country west of the Mississippi suited to their wants, to move to when they chose to emigrate, and to protect them there in their rights and possessions.
Articles 11 and 12: the cost of a six-chief delegation to explore the western country, and patents to the individuals named in the schedule.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that the 208,650 acres ceded by this treaty had a fair market value of $730,275 as of January 23, 1839, that the United States paid $339,611.00 for them, and that the disparity made the consideration unconscionable; it held the Miami entitled to $390,664.00 less offsets.

landTaken: The tract south of the Wabash between the western boundary of the big reserve near Pipe creek and the Mississinewa, with the 1818 reserves below the forks of the Wabash, opposite the Aboite and at Flat Rock creek, and the 1826 reserve at Seek's village (Royce areas 251 to 255). The Commission put the cession at 208,650 acres; the Me-to-sin-ia reserve (area 256) was excepted.
compensation: The Commission counted $339,611.00 as the consideration actually paid. A partial judgment of April 1, 1965 for this treaty and the 1834 treaty was vacated by the 1968 settlement of $1,373,000 net for the 1834, 1838 and 1840 treaties, accepted by both Miami plaintiffs.
today: The Commission found no fraud, duress or lack of fair and honorable dealings in the negotiation itself; its finding against the United States rests on the price. The settlement closed the claim in 1968. The country promised in Article 10 was set apart in Kansas by the treaty of November 28, 1840; the Miami were removed there in 1846.

plain.promised: $335,680 for Miami land in Indiana, a reserve kept for Me-to-sin-ia's band, matching improvements for those left behind, a boundary survey within a year, and a country west of the Mississippi guaranteed forever.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1964 that the 208,650 acres ceded were worth $730,275, that the United States paid $339,611.00, and that the price was unconscionable. It found no fraud in the negotiation itself.
plain.today: A 1968 settlement of $1,373,000 net, covering this and the 1834 and 1840 treaties, closed the claim. How much of it was for this treaty is not stated. The Miami were removed to Kansas in 1846.

nationVoice.summary: Diane Hunter, the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma's Tribal Historic Preservation Officer, writes that federal officials pressed the Myaamia to sell and move west, that traders' credit built debts payable only in land, that leaders agreed in 1838 only to consider removal, not to remove, and that the treaty led to the removal treaty of 1840.

openQuestions: treaties.json error: this entry is dated 1826-10-23 and named for that date, but its Kappler link (vol. 2, p. 519), its Royce pages (772-774) and Royce areas 251 to 256 are the treaty of November 6, 1838, which is what this file records.

treaties.json also lists Royce areas 329 and 330 in Kansas for this entry. Those are the Kansas reserve set apart by the 1840 treaty (and later dealt with in 1854), not land ceded or reserved by this treaty; they appear on kappler-539 and kappler-649 as well.

Finding 34 of the 1964 findings, as scanned, calls this 'the 1837 treaty' when stating the 208,650 acres and $730,275; finding 4 and the opinion make clear the November 6, 1838 treaty, effective January 23, 1839, is meant.
The 1968 settlement of $1,373,000 covers three treaties; how much of it was for this treaty is not stated.
Whether the Article 9 survey was made within a year was not researched.
